canonical_title: Damage tolerance for fracture critical components

versions.title_at_revision: Verify that all safety- and mission-critical parts are designed to be damage tolerant over the defined operational interval and duty cycle.
versions.text: Verify that all safety- and mission-critical parts are designed to be damage tolerant over the defined operational interval and duty cycle. DoD/MIL Doc: MIL-HDBK-1783B: A.4.7/A.5.7 through A.4.8.6/A.5.8.6 for application of damage tolerance and inspection methods FAA Doc: 14CFR references: 33.75

Criterion: Verify that all safety- and mission-critical parts are designed to be damage tolerant over the defined operational interval and duty cycle. Standard: a. Safety- and mission-critical engine parts maintain damage tolerance for two times (2X) the inspection interval in the presence of material, manufacturing, processing, and handling defects. b. Assumed initial surface flaw sizes are based on the non-destructive inspection (NDI) methods to be used during manufacture and depot maintenance. Assumed initial imbedded flaw sizes are based on the intrinsic material defect distribution or the NDI methods to be used during manufacture. Flaw size detection reliability is verified to have a probability of detection and confidence level of 90%/95% for manual inspections or 90%/50% for fully automated inspection methods. c. The residual strength is equal to the maximum stress that occurs during the design service life to the required design usage conditions. d. Safety and mission critical parts are serialized, properly marked and tracked, and subjected to the required process control and NDI procedures. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, test, demonstration, inspection and review of documentation. a. Fracture critical component: Damage tolerance analysis is conducted on each component classified as safety or mission critical. Damage tolerance analysis that addresses imbedded defects can be based on probabilistic methods that account for the distribution of variables. Analyses demonstrate that the assumed initial flaws will not grow to critical size for the usage, environment, and required damage tolerance operational period. The analyses account for repeated and sustained stresses, environments, and temperatures, and include the effects of load interactions. Analysis methods are verified by test, utilizing engine or spin pit testing. b. Initial flaw size: Controls and inspection methods are established through the damage tolerance control plan. Demonstration programs, in the absence of existing data, are performed to ensure that flaws greater than the assumed design flaws will not occur in finished components. Subsequent to successful completion of these demonstration programs, the selected inspection methods and processes become part of the production requirements and are not changed without approval of the Procuring Activity. c. Residual strength: Analyses verify that at the end of the required damage tolerance operational period, the strength requirement can be met for the flaw configuration and the required load. d. Damage tolerance controls: Inspection of drawings, specifications, and damage tolerance control plan verifies that parts are serialized, marked, tracked and comply with process and NDI controls. References: JSSG-2007: A.3.4.1.4, A.4.4.1.4 Parts classification; A.3.4.1.7, A.4.4.1.7 Damage tolerance; 3.4.1.7 through 3.4.1.7.4 and A.4.4.1.7 through A.4.4.1.7.4, Composites damage tolerance 14 CFR 33.75

versions.title_at_revision: Damage tolerance for fracture critical components
versions.text:
Standard: When operated, under steady state and transient conditions, IAW 7.3.1, fracture-critical engine parts resist failure caused by the presence of material, manufacturing, processing, maintenance, and service-induced defects, retaining residual strength to carry maximum limit stress, for twice the inspection interval defined in engine technical data without repair. Residual strength load conditions account for expected control system overspeed and engine deterioration. Fracture-critical parts are safety-critical or mission-critical components that achieve damage tolerance IAW MIL-STD-3024, Controlled Crack Growth (Fracture Analysis) paragraph. Initial surface flaw sizes are those detectable at the minimum demonstrated reliability (POD/CL) of the NDI methods used during manufacture and in-service maintenance. Initial embedded defect sizes and occurrence rates are characterized by exceedance curves (e.g., intrinsic material defect distributions) and controlled by material and processing controls and complementary NDI utilized during material processing and forming. Minimum flaw size detection POD/CL for all NDI methods is: a. Manual inspections: 90%/95%. b. Fully automated inspections 90%/50%. Material and processing controls, inclusive of the following, are established: a. Material and manufacturing operation specifications throughout the procurement and production chains. b. Allowable limits and controls for material property variation. c. Critical characteristics and defect sizes, locations, and orientations on product definition data. d. In-process and finished-part (production and in-service) NDI requirements and acceptance standards. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) For each fracture-critical part, review design documentation, engine life-management documentation, sustainment technical data, and product definition data that verifies compliance with material and processing control elements of this standard. Examples of such documentation include Durability and Damage Tolerance Control Plan, Engine Life Management Plan, PSIP Master Plan and Report, Technical Orders, NDI requirement definition, drawings and models, and material and processing specifications. Analysis.
  (1) Controlled crack growth (fracture mechanics) analysis is conducted for each component classified as fracture critical. Analyses account for repeated and sustained stresses, vibratory stress (including threshold value), and include the effects of load interactions. Stress intensity is based on the structural geometry and flaw geometry. The critical stress intensity is based on the required residual strength load level or vibratory stress threshold value, and temperature conditions that exist at the component location being analyzed. Analysis initial flaw sizes are defined by the demonstrated production and sustainment NDI capability, or by exceedance curves for embedded defects, established IAW this standard. Limit loads used for residual strength analysis are defined for each fracture-critical part. Embedded defect analysis can be based on probabilistic methods that account for the distribution of input variables. Demonstration.
    (1) Production NDI demonstrations are performed IAW MIL-HDBK-1823 to ensure that flaws larger than the analysis initial flaw size will not occur in finished components to the reliability level required by this standard. Test.
      (1) Lab test: Fracture-critical components are selected for verification by test (e.g., cyclic spin test, pressure cycling test). These components are either pre-flawed or contain natural flaws and are cycled to verify flaw growth characteristics.
      (2) Lab test: Full engine durability test or AMT/ASMET is conducted in a ground-based sea level test cell IAW JSSG-2007, Appendix A, Verification section, Endurance Tests paragraph. Tests include product-representative inlet conditions and extractions, and rotor imbalance. Tests are conducted using engine control software or schedules of the type design. Post-test teardown and NDI of hardware verifies predicted damage tolerance characteristics and ability to inspect IAW technical data. Minimum endurance test duration is twice the planned flight test duration. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Demonstration.
    (2) In-service NDI demonstrations are performed IAW MIL-HDBK-1823 to ensure that flaws larger than the corresponding analysis flaw size will not occur in released components to the reliability level required by this standard. In-service inspection flaw size detection capability is demonstrated on parts with prior engine operation time. Test.
    (3) Lab test: Full engine durability test or AMT/ASMET is conducted in a ground-based sea level test cell IAW JSSG-2007, Appendix A, Verification section, Endurance Tests paragraph. Tests include product-representative inlet conditions and extractions, and rotor imbalance. Tests are conducted using engine control software or schedules of the type design. Post-test teardown and NDI of hardware verifies predicted damage tolerance characteristics and ability to inspect IAW technical data. Minimum endurance test duration is the scheduled depot inspection interval or half the cold part DSL.
